fact: Tech Africa News reports that the Gates Foundation and OpenAI's $50 million Horizon1000 pilot, which applies AI tools to primary healthcare delivery in national health systems, will begin implementation in Rwanda, with scale-up to 1,000 clinics by 2028.

fact: BMZ Digital.Global says a method mapping agricultural land with satellite imagery and artificial intelligence, developed with the Rwanda Space Agency and the Ministry of Agriculture, is currently being tested in four districts.

fact: A MININFRA official says the ministry and the Rwanda Housing Authority released on 4 November 2025 an AI agent on Kubaka.gov.rw, the national building permits platform, that reviews design documents against the Building Code and zoning rules, with an instant yes or no for applicants promised only 'in the near future'.

ALX, Anthropic and the Government of Rwanda announce a Phase 2 pilot extending the Claude-based tutor Chidi to Rwanda's public education system, with up to 2,000 educators and higher learning institutions.

Vision Media reports that Rwanda is testing Tunga, an AI voice assistant integrated into the agriculture ministry's call centre that answers farmers' questions in Kinyarwanda, and that it correctly answered at least 60% of questions during testing.

The Global Fund case study says Rwanda uses AI in its public health system, with mobile vans screening for TB using AI software, computer-aided diagnostics reading digital chest X-rays to detect TB, and AI-assisted triage for TB case finding.
The Conversation's authors say Ethiopia and Rwanda used AI in TB and cervical cancer screening, in a regulatory vacuum.
